implementation.name: original-v1-h100-roofline-batch
implementation.scope: MLSysIM H100 (3.35 TB/s HBM, 989 TFLOP/s dense FP16, FP16 ridge 295.2 FLOP/byte) and the chapter's FP16 ResNet-50 classifier head (2,048 to 1,000, one read of input and weights, one write of output). Only the classifier marker moves; all other printed points, ceilings, and ridges stay. INT8 is not used for this marker. Attainable throughput is the roofline bound, not a measured rate; motion is not time; batching's latency cost is qualitative.
implementation.question: Where does batching move the classifier on the H100 roofline?

purpose: Change only the classifier head's batch and watch its printed FP16 marker slide down to batch 1, climb the bandwidth slope, cross the FP16 ridge at the first computed batch, then sit on the flat ceiling while intensity keeps rising.
storyboard: Printed point: batch 32, 30.5 FLOP/byte, 102.3 TFLOP/s (10.3% of peak), bandwidth bound; the marker coincides with the printed dot.
Batch 1: 1.0 FLOP/byte, 3.3 TFLOP/s; weights are nearly all the traffic; lands on GPT-2 XL batch-1 decode.
Batch 256: 185.4 FLOP/byte, 621.0 TFLOP/s; FLOPs grow, weight bytes fixed; still on the slope.
Batch 512: 290.6 FLOP/byte, not 512; activation bytes grow; still below the 295.2 FLOP/byte ridge at 98.4% of peak.
Batch 527: first batch past the FP16 ridge (295.3 FLOP/byte); binding term switches to the 989 TFLOP/s ceiling.
Batch 1,024: 405.7 FLOP/byte but the bound stays 989 TFLOP/s; the limit for this layer is 671.9 FLOP/byte; the cost is waiting for a batch to form (no latency number).
guard: The verified PNG is unchanged; overlays use its intrinsic pixel axes, measured and asserted in calc.py, and the batch-32 stop is asserted to sit on the printed marker's centroid. Every displayed value comes from MLSysIM (Hardware.Cloud.H100 and Scenarios.ResNet50ClassifierHeadBatch32.variant(batch_size=B).traffic_intensity); batch 32 equals DenseLayerAnalysisCalc.dense_ai. The crossing batch is computed, not read from the plot. No slider on GPT-2 decode, no INT8 placement of the classifier, no latency or per-request throughput claim.
